findings.statement: CA9 is a surface protein with a known-target control status and a moderate conjugate suitability score [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.647]. Only a minority of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=24.3%], staining in a vital organ (stomach) is at the highest level, GTEx proteome flags stomach enrichment, and CSPA did not observe it at the surface. Kidney staining is zero; a high score does not show a conjugate would work.

CD70 has the best suitability among the controls [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746] with a surface call and no enrichment in vital-organ proteome. In the weakest quarter of donors only a small fraction of tumour cells express it [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=17.7%], and staining data are not available, so normal-tissue safety is unassessed by this layer.

ENPP3 is a surface protein (CSPA high confidence) with intermediate suitability [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.578], but kidney staining is at the highest level [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; kidney_staining_level=3.0] and duodenum staining is also high, an on-target off-tumour concern for a kidney cancer conjugate.

SCARB1 tops the target convergence ranking, yet as a conjugate target it is weak: very few tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1%], adrenal staining is high, kidney staining is moderate, and the GTEx proteome shows adrenal enrichment [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.08].

SLC16A3 has high conjugate suitability [gene=SLC16A3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.725] and the most homogeneous tumour expression of the set, measured in the weakest quarter of donors [gene=SLC16A3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=43.7%]. It is a multi-pass transporter with a short extracellular part, adrenal staining is high and CSPA did not observe it, so a conjugate is uncertain; a small-molecule route may suit it better.

CA9 expression is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336], but the arms do not differ after adjustment [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917]. This is a lead only, not a predictor.

NNMT shows a weak association with earlier progression on nivolumab in the nivolumab-versus-everolimus trial [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_checkmate025.log_hr_per_sd=0.083], with no difference between the two drugs after adjustment [gene=NNMT; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_nivolumab_vs_everolimus.padj=0.999]. No IMmotion arm was returned for NNMT; trial data give no usable signal.

PSAT1 is associated with earlier progression on nivolumab [gene=PSAT1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_checkmate025.log_hr_per_sd=0.204] but not significantly after adjustment [gene=PSAT1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.nivolumab_checkmate025.padj=0.67]; the direction is the same in the other arms, and none differs between arms after correction. Its biomarker value rests on tumour-versus-normal and prognosis, not on treatment response.

EPAS1 is associated with longer benefit on everolimus [gene=EPAS1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.everolimus_checkmate025.log_hr_per_sd=-0.183], but nothing is significant after correction and the nivolumab-versus-everolimus difference is not significant.

Immune cells make most CD70 tumour transcripts [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654], and it correlates with CD8 T cells, so CD70 is partly an immune-compartment signal and not purely tumour cell. On atezolizumab plus bevacizumab, higher CD70 is associated with longer benefit [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; log_hr_atezolizumab_bevacizumab=-0.383], an association only.

Immune cells make essentially all FCGR3A tumour transcripts [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.999] and it correlates strongly with the xCell immune score [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_immune_score=0.795]. Its tumour increase is infiltration, not a tumour-cell target.

PSAT1 is not a subgroup target candidate. It is higher in BAP1-mutant tumours in TCGA RNA [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711] but the CPTAC protein difference is not significant, and it is higher in ccB than ccA [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=2.364], so it tracks the aggressive ccB state.

CA9 is the one flagged subgroup target candidate here: higher in PBRM1-mutant tumours in TCGA RNA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148] and in CPTAC RNA, with a smaller protein difference [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_protein.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=0.335]. The effect is modest, so PBRM1-directed use is hypothesis-level.

EPAS1 defines the ccA/ccB split and is lower in ccB in TCGA RNA [gene=EPAS1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-0.935]; no mutation-based subgroup candidate flag. Its subtype signal is partly circular because the split uses it.

NNMT is assigned to tumour cells in both single-cell datasets, with tumour-cell share [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.97] in the first and [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.948] in the second. The attribution holds, though paired donors in the second set are few.

The cell attribution of SCARB1 does not replicate: the dominant group is myeloid in the first dataset and tumour cell in the second, with tumour-cell share [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.336] versus [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.582]. It is expressed in several compartments, which weakens the case for a tumour-specific target.

PCK1 is tumour-cell dominant in both single-cell datasets and lower in tumour than proximal tubule in both [gene=PCK1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_vs_tubule_log2fc=-5.787] and [gene=PCK1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_vs_tubule_log2fc=-3.044]. Loss of tubular identity is consistent across datasets; this makes it a loss marker, not a drug target.

NNMT protein replicates in the confirmatory cohort in the same direction and with significance [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776]; the fold-change size differs by technology and should not be compared.

PSAT1 protein is lower in tumours in the confirmatory cohort too [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946]. The single phosphosite measured in both cohorts did not replicate.

SCARB1 protein replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334], on fewer matched pairs than NNMT, so the tumour increase is robust even though the adc and cell-attribution layers are weak.
CA9 was not tested in the confirmatory cohort (absent or too sparse there, fewer than the required matched tumour-normal pairs). This is a coverage gap, not a failure to replicate.

PCK1 protein is lower in tumours in the confirmatory cohort [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-4.819] and both phosphosites measured in both cohorts replicate.

SLC16A3 protein replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=SLC16A3; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=3.551] and its one measured phosphosite also replicates.

HK2 protein does not replicate in the confirmatory cohort: it is up in discovery protein [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_discovery_log2fc=2.106] but not significantly changed, and in the opposite direction, in the confirmatory cohort [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256]. The tool reports that it does not replicate, so its high target rank rests on RNA and discovery protein alone.

caveats: No gene differs between trial arms after correction; all treatment findings are associations from small arms and are leads, not predictors.
ADC scores combine topology, staining and single-cell homogeneity; they do not show that a conjugate or radioligand would work. Staining data were missing for CD70.
Single-cell attribution comes from two datasets with few paired donors.
The confirmatory cohort uses a different technology; judge direction and significance, not fold-change size. CA9 was not tested there.
PSAT1 and PCK1 are lower in tumours, so they are loss biomarkers, not inhibitor or conjugate targets.
Not run for lack of call budget: sc/confirmatory checks for ENPP3 and CD70, treatment_response for CD70 and ENPP3 beyond the immune_profile hazard ratio.
